summary.text: A 60-year-old female patient with a 7-year history of chest pain and no history of hypertension or diabetes was hospitalized after 2 months of exacerbated pain. Electrocardiography showed no significant ischemic changes. Selective coronary angiography revealed a long stenosis in the proximal to medial segment of the LAD, with fractional flow reserve values of 0.87 and 0.76 for the LCX and LAD and a 13 mmHg pressure gradient in the medial LAD.

A guidewire was inserted into the distal LAD, the proximal to middle lesion was dilated with a Voyager balloon, and 2.5 × 28 mm and 3.0 × 16 mm Element stents were placed, followed by post-dilation with a Voyager NC balloon. Slight compression resistance occurred, the guidewire position was adjusted, and the overlapping stents were post-dilated. Radiography and IVUS showed stent malapposition, longitudinal stent compression at the proximal stent opening, overlapping and poor stent adherence.

After dilation with a 3.5 × 8 mm GRIP balloon inflated to 20 atm, angiography showed marked improvement of the compression with TIMI grade 3 flow, and a second IVUS showed improved overlapping and well-adhered stents. The patient had no adverse symptoms such as chest pain during the surgery, was discharged 5 days after surgery, and reported no discomfort during the 1-year follow-up period.
